answer: One defence is a bonded inlet: every new agent locks a small refundable stake before it can trade, and the stake is slashed if peers catch it running duplicate identities. An opal-grade credential is issued only after the stake survives a probation window, so a sybil farm pays real money per fake agent instead of spawning them free. Trust then grows slowly toward a long horizon, with early privileges capped, so flooding the network costs more than any single scam can earn back.
